# Independent audit of the opposite-singular-core 8/17 cap exclusion



## Geometry and exact data

The two collinearities give A=Br/(B+r) and a=bt/(b+t), with positive denominators. The four core sectors then yield k=x+y+U+V and the three exact cap masses y+U, y+V, x+Z. The relation UV=PQ is an algebraic identity in the four actual radii. The formula for Z in terms of xi=B/r retains the same body; it is not an independent marginal assignment. Dropping the nontrivial PSD upper bounds is a relaxation in the correct direction.

If a cap is at least half the body, the 8/17 conclusion is immediate. Otherwise the two largest-direction inequalities imply Z<min(U,V). The simultaneous swap U,V and xi->p/xi preserves Z exactly. With U>=V, the inequality Z<V gives (U-V)xi<V-Up and hence U<Q. The product UV=PQ then gives P<V<=U<Q, so all denominators and later interval restrictions follow rigorously.

## Scalar minimum

I independently checked the exact square identity (6) for Z-Z0 by common-denominator expansion. Its denominator is strictly positive. Under the restrictions above, U+V<P+Q<2Q, making Z0 positive. Equivalently, minimizing Z over xi gives the positive stationary point

    xi*=P(Q-U)/[Q(U-P)],

and the same value P(2Q-U-V)/(Q-P); the derivative changes from negative to positive there.

For fixed y, the largest-cap quotient decreases until x=y+T-Z and increases after it, because its two branch derivatives have the printed strict signs. Ignoring the lower bound x>=P therefore only lowers the possible minimum. The derivative with respect to y has sign min(U,V)-Z>0, so y>=Q is used correctly. Replacing Z by its lower bound increases the denominator, again lowering the relaxed quotient.

After Q=1, the denominator in (9) is positive. The derivative numerator can be written

    P(1-P)(1-T)(3T+1),

with the positive squared denominator in (10), so the expression is nondecreasing on sqrt(P)<=T<1. At T=sqrt(P)=s, cancellation of the positive factor 1-s gives (1+s)^2/(s^2+5s+2). The final square (3s-1)^2/[17(s^2+5s+2)] proves the lower bound exactly, including equality in the relaxed scalar problem.

Finally 8/17-128/279=56/4743 is positive. Boundary strata with zero sector excess are included, since the proof only used weak core lower bounds. The generalized-normal normalization is an ordinary invertible planar map, scales every area by one determinant, and makes no mixed-lattice claim.

## Why the earlier half-cap guess was insufficient

The exact actual hexagon in Section 11 of `candidate 1a5bfc0fdb9108c3` has all three cap fractions below 1/2, so that stronger guess was false. It is consistent with this theorem: its largest cap fraction is 58/117>8/17. Its actual coordinates, sector areas, cap areas, strict turns, and boundary ray points are independently checked with 25 exact rational assertions in `supporting computation verify_type_b_hexagon_half_cap_obstruction_defect_transport.py`. That example is not a cap-band, profile, criticality, or Lorentz counterexample.
